To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a SF/sub 5/--H/sub 6/ radiation-chemical lasing system operating at pressures up 10 atm has been developed.

a radiation-chemical SF/sub 6/ laser was initiated by a fast electron beam from a field-emission high-voltage coaxial diode and that the energy parameters of the laser radiation were measured at pressures up to ten atmospheres.
a radiation-chemical laser with a high-pressure SF/sub 6/-H/sub 2/mixture was initiated by an intense pulsed electron beam from a coaxially arranged field emission diode.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (1) the development and study of a coaxial field-emission diode for the generation of high-current electron beams; (2) the development of a radiation-chemical laser for the generation of pulsed laser radiation at high pressure; and (3) the development of an optical system for the delivery of the laser radiation to the target.
the use of high-voltage coaxial field emission diodes for the initiation of radiation-chemical lasers.
the development of high-pressure SF/sub 6/ radiation-chemical lasers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the laser was initiated by the electron beam and that the energy parameters of the laser radiation were determined by the electron beam parameters.
the laser radiation is generated as a result of the chemical reactions between excited SF/sub 6/ and H/sub 2/.

the authors have demonstrated that a high-pressure radiation-chemical SF/sub 6/ laser can be initiated with an electron beam from a field-emission diode and that this laser is capable of producing high specific energy outputs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the radiation-chemical laser is a promising source of high-power laser radiation in a broad range of pressures.

the energy characteristics of a radiation-chemical laser can be substantially improved if a fast electron beam from a field-emission diode is used to initiate a SF/sub 7/:H/sub 7/=70:1 active mixture at a pressure up to 10 atmospheres.
the radiation-chemical laser is a powerful tool for the generation of high-power laser radiation in the 1--3-mu range.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the efficiency of conversion of electron beam energy into radiation chemical laser radiation increases with increasing pressure.

the efficiency of conversion of electron beam energy into the laser radiation was 2-3 times greater than in the case of a radiation-chemical laser excited by an electron beam from a diode with a plane cathode.
the energy parameters of the radiation-chemical laser were significantly improved by increasing the pressure of the working medium.
